objective: Audit SQLite-native live-drift signals for WP206 same-inode data/schema mutation detection, separating ephemeral cache invalidation from durable restart/recovery identity.

f2_source_observations.observation: The restart-stable FRANKENSTEIN2_UNIFIEDDB_BOUND_FILE_AUTHORITY/v1 receipt intentionally hashes only canonical_db_path, db_device and db_inode. It therefore remains stable across same-inode content mutation.

UnifiedDBFingerprint/v2 already records mutable main-file sha256, schema digest/version, user_version, page count, journal mode and WAL/SHM presence, but its own classification says SQLITE_MAIN_FILE_IDENTITY_NOT_STATE_SNAPSHOT. The immutable=1 schema probe intentionally excludes uncheckpointed WAL state.
G4 checks path/device/inode plus checkpoint digest and performs BEGIN IMMEDIATE + CAS on the stored authority receipt; the accepted next discriminator is same-inode live data/schema drift.

external_primary_sources.finding: PRAGMA data_version changes on a connection when another connection commits. It does not change for commits made by the same connection, and values from different connections are not comparable.
schema_version is an internal schema cookie incremented when schema changes. It is a schema invalidation signal, not a complete data mutation witness; manually forcing it is unsafe.
The main-file change counter is useful for cache invalidation in rollback-journal operation, but SQLite explicitly notes it might not increment on every transaction in WAL mode.
WAL-index iChange increments per transaction but belongs to transient shared-memory coordination state, not a portable durable restart identity.
update_hook is registered on a specific SQLite connection and has documented coverage gaps; it is not a cross-process durable mutation identity primitive.

supported: PRAGMA data_version is suitable as a low-cost EPHEMERAL foreign-writer invalidation witness only when sampled on the same long-lived connection at two times.
PRAGMA schema_version can complement it as a schema-change sentinel, but does not witness arbitrary data mutations.
Neither data_version nor schema_version should be folded into the restart-stable WP206 bound-file authority receipt.
The main-file header change counter is insufficient as a universal mutation sequence under WAL.
F2 already deliberately separates restart-stable file authority from the richer mutable UnifiedDB fingerprint; that separation should be preserved.
not_supported: SQLite exposes a built-in persistent globally comparable monotonic data-version suitable for WP206 recovery identity.
data_version values can be persisted and compared across reopened connections as an authority proof.
schema_version alone proves that canonical data did not change.
main-file hashing with immutable=1 observes uncheckpointed WAL state.

hypothesis: A separate ephemeral live-drift witness can detect concurrent same-inode mutation without destabilizing the durable file-authority receipt.
counterhypothesis: WP206 checkpoint digest + transactional locking already close all relevant same-inode drift hazards; adding a live-drift witness would only add false invalidations and complexity.
next_discriminator: Map exactly which WP206 read/recovery boundaries can be invalidated by another connection while preserving valid unrelated writes, and determine whether data_version/schema_version should remain diagnostics only or become a typed pre/post-transaction guard. This requires a separate E2 claim.

efficiency.candidate_runtime_cost: Two bounded PRAGMA reads at selected boundaries if promoted; not yet promoted.
